title: Can Stock Market Forecasters Forecast?
question: Do professional forecasters and newsletters beat chance?
changed: Scored thousands of recommendations: their record was no better than random, and arguably worse.

title: A Random-Difference Series for Use in the Analysis of Time Series
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
question: Do commodity price series contain patterns, or just accumulated noise?
changed: Cumulated random differences look like price charts, trends and all: the random walk as a benchmark.

title: The Analysis of Economic Time-Series—Part I: Prices
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series A (General)
question: Do weekly stock and commodity prices have predictable cycles?
changed: Serial correlations were near zero: prices seemed to wander like a random walk.

title: Stock-Market "Patterns" and Financial Analysis: Methodological Suggestions
question: Would chartists see their patterns in purely random data?
changed: Simulated random walks produce head-and-shoulders and other chart patterns; analysis should start from changes, not levels.

title: The Behavior of Stock-Market Prices
question: Are daily stock price changes independent and normal?
changed: Dow stocks: changes nearly independent but fat-tailed, supporting Mandelbrot's stable laws.

title: Proof That Properly Anticipated Prices Fluctuate Randomly
question: Why should a competitive futures price be unpredictable?
changed: If prices fully reflect expectations, price changes are a martingale: randomness as a sign of efficiency, not chaos.

verified.note: Industrial Management Review (1965) has no registered DOI; only later reprints do.

title: The Adjustment of Stock Prices to New Information
question: How quickly do prices absorb news like stock splits?
changed: Invented the event study: abnormal returns around splits show prices adjust before and at the news.

title: Efficient Capital Markets: A Review of Theory and Empirical Work
question: What does it mean for prices to fully reflect information, and is it true?
changed: Defined weak, semi-strong and strong efficiency and showed any test is joint with a model of expected returns.

title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
question: How do people actually choose between risky prospects?
changed: Gains and losses from a reference point, loss aversion and distorted probabilities replace expected utility of wealth.

title: On the Impossibility of Informationally Efficient Markets
question: If prices reveal everything, who pays to gather information?
changed: Perfect efficiency is self-defeating; prices must stay noisy enough to pay informed traders for their costs.

verified.note: Crossref has no DOI for American Economic Review articles of this period.

title: Do Stock Prices Move Too Much to be Justified by Subsequent Changes in Dividends?
question: Is stock price volatility consistent with rational forecasts of dividends?
changed: Prices are far more volatile than the ex-post present value of dividends allows: excess volatility.

verified.note: Crossref has no DOI for American Economic Review articles of this period; the 1980 NBER working paper (w0456) does.

title: Does the Stock Market Overreact?
question: Do investors overreact to dramatic news?
changed: Three-to-five-year losers subsequently beat past winners: long-horizon reversal.

title: The Dividend-Price Ratio and Expectations of Future Dividends and Discount Factors
question: What does the dividend yield tell us about future returns and dividend growth?
changed: A log-linear identity splits the dividend yield into expected returns and expected dividend growth: the basis of valuation-ratio forecasting.

title: Mean reversion in stock prices: Evidence and implications
question: Do stock prices have a transitory component that mean-reverts?
changed: Variance ratios show negative autocorrelation at long horizons, with low power, which they faced honestly.

title: Stock Market Prices do not Follow Random Walks: Evidence from a Simple Specification Test
question: Is the random walk rejected by weekly returns?
changed: A heteroskedasticity-robust variance-ratio test rejects the random walk, driven by small stocks' positive autocorrelation.

title: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?
question: Why do prices keep drifting after earnings surprises?
changed: The drift isn't a risk premium; prices underreact to earnings news.

title: Noise Trader Risk in Financial Markets
question: Can irrational traders survive and move prices?
changed: Noise traders' unpredictability is itself a risk that deters arbitrage, so they can earn more and persist.

title: Simple Technical Trading Rules and the Stochastic Properties of Stock Returns
question: Do simple moving-average and range-break rules predict stock returns?
changed: On the Dow from 1897 to 1986, returns after the rules' buy signals beat those after sell signals, by more than standard return models explain.

title: The Limits of Arbitrage
question: Why don't professional arbitrageurs eliminate mispricing?
changed: Arbitrageurs use other people's money; losses trigger withdrawals exactly when the trade is best.

title: A model of investor sentiment
question: Can one model give both underreaction and overreaction?
changed: Investors switch between believing earnings trend and believing they revert: momentum short-run, reversal long-run.

title: Investor Psychology and Security Market Under- and Overreactions
question: What if traders are overconfident about their private signals?
changed: Overconfidence and biased self-attribution produce short-run momentum and long-run reversal.

title: Valuation Ratios and the Long-Run Stock Market Outlook
question: What do high price ratios say about the market's long-run returns?
changed: The dividend yield and the ten-year smoothed P/E had forecast ten-year real returns, and the high ratios of the late 1990s implied poor ones to come.

title: Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors
question: How do individual investors who trade actively perform?
changed: The most active households underperformed the market by several points a year, mostly through costs; overconfidence explains the trading.

title: The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis
question: Can efficiency and behavioral finance be reconciled?
changed: Markets as ecologies: efficiency varies over time as strategies compete, adapt and die out.

title: A Comprehensive Look at The Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
question: Do the popular predictors of the equity premium work out of sample?
changed: Almost none beat the historical mean out of sample; in-sample success was unstable.

title: Predicting Excess Stock Returns Out of Sample: Can Anything Beat the Historical Average?
question: Can predictors of the equity premium beat the historical mean out of sample once forecasts are held to what theory allows?
changed: Setting a wrong-signed slope to zero and flooring the forecast at zero turns several predictors' out-of-sample R² positive, small but worth having to an investor.

title: Out-of-Sample Equity Premium Prediction: Combination Forecasts and Links to the Real Economy
question: Can the failed predictors work together?
changed: Averaging many individual forecasts beats the historical mean out of sample, and the gains line up with the business cycle.

title: CAPE and the COVID-19 Pandemic Effect
question: How should CAPE be read when long-term interest rates are this low?
changed: It read CAPE valuations against long-term interest rates, across the US, UK, Europe, Japan and China, through the 2020 pandemic.
